input.rationale: Tidy the parent's next-question list now that the trim consumer it named has been settled by the child account: the answer is that the drifted values do change the trim bound and trim acts on it (witnessed: compacted index 7 over six indices of content, receipt ec3329dc273e452aa92bcd44652c116a), with the snapshot path reaching the same class of consequence through the drifted decided index. The parent's discriminator therefore keeps only the questions an execution can still settle - whether anything inside the sealed configuration bounds or repairs the drift after many more rounds or a later leader change - while the handoff item stays as the sourced narrowing recorded earlier and the trim/snapshot consumers are now recorded in their own child accounts.

investigations.discriminator: Whether anything inside the sealed configuration bounds or repairs the drift - a counter or storage limit, or a later leader change - after many more re-synchronization rounds; the decisive observation would be the reported accepted and decided indices and the readable decided log after further rounds and further leader changes. The library's own reconfiguration handoff is already narrowed out (the StopSign carries only the next configuration and metadata while the documented flow builds the new instance with fresh storage), and the drifted values' effect on the compaction paths is settled in the trim and snapshot child accounts.

investigations.question: When a replica that has already accepted its configuration's StopSign is re-synchronized by the leader (PrepareReq -> Prepare -> Promise -> AcceptSync, e.g. after a re-established connection), does its reported accepted index stay within its actual log content, so that the StopSign keeps being observable as decided (decided index == accepted index) and the decided log keeps being readable?
investigations.hypothesis: No. create_log_sync passes the follower's accepted index (which already counts its stored StopSign as one index) as LogSync.sync_idx; sync_log sets accepted_idx = sync_idx + suffix.len() and then adds 1 again because the LogSync carries the StopSign, so the re-synchronized replica's accepted index becomes one larger than its log content while its decided index stays at the real StopSign position. The replica then reports the inflated index in Accepted, so a write quorum of inflated reports lets the leader set a decided index beyond the entries it can read.
investigations.discriminator: Whether the drift is bounded by anything inside the sealed configuration (a counter or storage limit, or a repair triggered by a later leader change), whether it transfers through the library's own reconfiguration handoff (narrowed: the StopSign carries only the next configuration and metadata while the documented flow builds the new instance with fresh storage and requires the user to supply the application state), and whether further producers of compaction exist; the decisive observations would be the reported indexes after many more rounds, a later leader change, and any compaction path not yet exercised.

gaps.question: Which legitimate producer path can hand a leader a LogSync whose sync_idx already covers the sender's own StopSign, i.e. whose receiver's accepted index is inflated by the unconditional +1?

investigations.question: Does the drifted accepted index reach the trim decision? The leader derives its trim index from the minimum of the accepted indexes it has recorded for the configuration's nodes, and those recorded values are exactly the ones the re-synchronization inflates; the documented contract instead requires that all nodes have decided the trim index. Does a drifted minimum let trim remove entries that a replica has not decided, or push the compacted index past the entries a replica still holds?
investigations.hypothesis: Once every node's recorded accepted index is inflated above its content, the minimum the leader uses exceeds the cluster's true minimum content index, so trim can accept a trim index that some replica has not decided (against the documented requirement) and can push the compacted index past that replica's entries; a later re-synchronization of such a replica would then ask the storage for a suffix starting below the compacted index, which the in-memory storage computes by subtracting the compacted index and would underflow.
investigations.discriminator: Whether any producer other than the two trim paths can raise a compacted index past a truthful replica's recorded report in the same configuration (for example a forwarded compaction, a snapshot-driven compaction or a store-level trim), and whether a caller or storage can request a prefix below a compacted index by a route this cluster does not use; the decisive observation would be a compacted index above a truthful replica's content or a panic or silently empty suffix on such a request.

investigations.question: Does the snapshot path let a drifted decided index compact past the entries a replica still holds? The documented note says only up to the decided index can be snapshotted, and the implementation compares the user's index against the leader's decided index and then builds a snapshot from the storage range that starts at the current compacted index; both of those values can be inflated by the same drift, so a snapshot request can be accepted for an index above the entries in the log.
investigations.hypothesis: After the drift, snapshot(Some(index)) is accepted for an index up to the drifted decided index, and the snapshot is created from a storage range whose start is at or near the empty part of the log, so the resulting snapshot contains none of the entries a replica holds while the compacted index is advanced past them; readers of the decided region then see the snapshot instead of the entries, and the entries are no longer reachable through the log.
investigations.discriminator: Whether the peers that receive a forwarded snapshot request, and a follower called directly, show the same empty snapshot in their own reads; the derivation says they compute the same bound and range on their own decided index, so a decisive observation would be their snapshots and their reads after the call sampled directly.

investigations.question: Does the drifted accepted index reach the trim decision? The leader derives its trim index from the minimum of the accepted indexes it has recorded for the configuration's nodes, and those recorded values are exactly the ones the re-synchronization inflates; the documented contract instead requires that all nodes have decided the trim index. Does a drifted minimum let trim remove entries that a replica has not decided, or push the compacted index past the entries a replica still holds?
investigations.hypothesis: Once every node's recorded accepted index is inflated above its content, the minimum the leader uses exceeds the cluster's true minimum content index, so trim can accept a trim index that some replica has not decided (against the documented requirement) and can push the compacted index past that replica's entries; a later re-synchronization of such a replica would then ask the storage for a suffix starting below the compacted index, which the in-memory storage computes by subtracting the compacted index and would underflow.
investigations.discriminator: Whether any producer other than the two trim paths can raise a compacted index past a truthful replica's recorded report in the same configuration (for example a forwarded compaction, a snapshot-driven compaction or a store-level trim), and whether a caller or storage can request a prefix below a compacted index by a route this cluster does not use; the decisive observation would be a compacted index above a truthful replica's content or a panic or silently empty suffix on such a request.

investigations.question: Does the snapshot path let a drifted decided index compact past the entries a replica still holds? The documented note says only up to the decided index can be snapshotted, and the implementation compares the user's index against the leader's decided index and then builds a snapshot from the storage range that starts at the current compacted index; both of those values can be inflated by the same drift, so a snapshot request can be accepted for an index above the entries in the log.
investigations.hypothesis: After the drift, snapshot(Some(index)) is accepted for an index up to the drifted decided index, and the snapshot is created from a storage range whose start is at or near the empty part of the log, so the resulting snapshot contains none of the entries a replica holds while the compacted index is advanced past them; readers of the decided region then see the snapshot instead of the entries, and the entries are no longer reachable through the log.
investigations.discriminator: Whether the peers that receive a forwarded snapshot request, and a follower called directly, show the same empty snapshot in their own reads; the derivation says they compute the same bound and range on their own decided index, so a decisive observation would be their snapshots and their reads after the call sampled directly.
